results.label: thm:main
results.title: Main theorem
results.note: The full main conclusion is proved with one absolute positive logarithmic constant, all natural-valued sparse degree sequences, the actual independent uniform row-slice model, characteristic roots with algebraic multiplicity, and the literal variance normalization sqrt(d*(1-d/n)). results.label: thm:intro-intermediate
results.title: Intermediate singular values
results.note: Introductory restatement of thm:intermediate. Full intermediate singular-value theorem for the literal square matrix M_n-z*sqrt(d)*I. The target quantifies over every fixed complex z, every sigma in (0,1), every sufficiently large lower logarithmic constant and every degree sequence eventually in the literal lower band. Its exact rounded count is q0=floor(n/d^3)-1+2*ceil(n/d^2); q0<n and q0<=5*n/d^2 hold eventually, so the positive source scale constant Cq=5 works. Lean position n-q0-1 is the one-based manuscript position n-q0. The actual surviving submatrix has N-t rows and exactly t+1 singular values at or below that position. The checked bad-row Markov and row-deletion event has failure at most 2*R/d without independence between distance events. The actual retained shifted matrix negative second moment and inverse-square tail counting give s_j>=exp(-R*d^(1/96))/d. A coordinate isometry and spectral subspace dimension argument prove principal Hermitian eigenvalue comparison. The actual retained row Gram is a principal submatrix of the full A A* product, whose spectrum is nonnegative; this transfers the bound to the actual full square matrix. This principal row-Gram route proves the same inequality as the manuscript column-Gram increment route. Uniform log(d)<=d^(1/96) absorbs the polynomial factor into radius constant R+1. One dimension threshold covers the full fixed spectral window and source band, yielding the explicit uniform B/d failure estimate with B=2*R. Logarithmic degree divergence and a checked squeeze prove the literal success probability 1-o(1) along every allowed degree sequence. Both the introductory and Section 7 statements use this same complete proof, and no mathematical estimate remains a proof argument. The supporting scalar deletion budget q0*d*log(d)/n<=5*log(d)/d tends to zero, The exact relative-scale identity also gives q0/(n/(d*log(d))) tending to zero, verifying the finer deletion scale used in Section 9. All earlier structural, random-normal, omitted-row, distance, Gram and spectral dependencies are checked proofs. The circular-law theorem and the remaining Section 8-9 results are not discharged by this result.

results.label: prop:LLTTY-package
results.title: Author-derived deterministic consequences of the LLTTY decomposition
results.note: The complete five-part author-derived LLTTY proposition is proved in the standing manuscript setting, with one uniform dimension threshold and common positive constants. Part (i): the literal Ku/Pv families retain the actual spread-mass condition and original exponential part-height threshold. Real and imaginary quantiles construct separated cohorts from the exact normalized gradual class, at the source k>=5/theta0 scale. Exact floor refinement, majority-level survival and prefix mass, the nine-cell greedy spread bound, and accumulated factor-two contractions yield the exact decomposition S = union(4 <= u <= v) Ku union Pv. Positive absolute choices cK=1/4608 and cP=1/65536 work uniformly for every v>=5, every codimension parameter, and every degree above C*log(n), once n is large. The proved shrink threshold n3/656 is absorbed in those constants; the external Lemma 5.9 numerical threshold n3/192 is not claimed. Part (ii): uniformly in the standing logarithmic lower band, both admissible codimensions, and every integer scale 1<=k<=sqrt(n)/d^(3/2), the actual approximation family is finite, has at most exp(n) coordinate-multiset classes, and every restricted family obeys the same count. Multiset equality is equivalent to coordinate permutation; injective part/value encoding proves the class-size formula. The four actual rank blocks and finite grid alphabets give a direct proof in the manuscript setting for 0<a3<=1/65536; the broader degree scope of external Lemma 5.1 is not claimed. Part (iii): actual canonical and ordered canonical profiles satisfy local factorial compression with constant 4096 and small-bin coordinate-union mass at most 512*T, including T=d^(-kappa)*n. Part (iv): actual spread coordinate mass equals the ordered profile spread mass. The cutoff kappa=cK*a3/16 gives the exact K1/K2 mass alternatives. K1 yields a height/weight product at most d^(-(cK*a3/32)*n), with the floor in n3 controlled once a3*n>=4, and the actual class entropy consequence. K2 uses actual integer coordinate quantiles and the 512*T per-bin mass bound to give both probability tails at least cK*a3/32 and a gap at least (cK*a3/16384)*d^kappa. A single dimension threshold works for every degree above C*log(n), every scale and every codimension; the combined branch conclusion uses the common positive decay/gap constant cK*a3/16384, with C=1 in the product estimate. The original heights product times inverse weights product is exactly the checked ratio product. Part (v): every actual closed coordinate cluster of radius at most d^(-v) gives low-tail mass delta/36 at floor(log_2(72*sqrt(d)/delta)). A repeated rounded value and the last nonempty level chunk prove this without a cluster-to-level assumption. For s=cP*a3 and the literal height threshold H, actual high-height coordinates below H/(d*sqrt(s)) occupy only a bounded interval of actual small-part bins. Their mass is at most 512*(2-log_2(s)/2)*d^(-1/3)*n, hence at most s*n/4 uniformly at large degree. The remaining high-height population gives high-tail mass s/4. Exact logarithms and integer floors give the manuscript gap s*(v-4)/2 under its original separation hypothesis, with no strengthened hypothesis. The full target retains delta<=36*cP*a3, both codimensions, the displayed class-count scale conditions, and every part of the package. The common constants are cK=1/4608, cP=1/65536, c0=cP*a3/4, c1=cK*a3/16384 and C=4096, for every fixed 0<a3<=1/65536. The actual alternating greedy exposure, graph probability, conditional drift, both source floors, ambient minor normalization, vanishing initial retained-zero probability and fixed-fraction asymptotic errors discharge every input to the common slow-cutoff squeeze.
